raised_by: wq#787 (verify-pass of wq#763/PR#53), fixed under wq#841
frozen_file_status: UNCHANGED — byte-identical to the 2026-08-22 artifact, sha256 still verifies. This errata sits beside it; it does not amend it.
reproduction_check_2026-08-23: Re-running the shipped script against the live queue.db with the same fixed cutoff (2026-08-21 18:06:42) reproduces every field above exactly. rework_rate is the ONLY divergence.

field_in_error.why_it_moved: The rule was `notes LIKE '%REOPENED%'`. notes is a mutable field that `wq done` REPLACES wholesale on every close, so a ticket that was genuinely reopened silently left the population the next time anyone closed it. created_at (what the population is keyed on) never changed, so nothing in the artifact showed the loss. Roughly 14 of ~18 markers fleet-wide evaporated in under 24h from ordinary ticket churn, not from any reduction in rework. Two more were observed vanishing during the wq#841 fix itself (wq#755 and wq#760, both re-closed mid-session).
field_in_error.secondary_defect: SQLite LIKE is case-insensitive for ASCII, so prose counted too: of the 3 rows matching the rule on 2026-08-23, wq#645 ('wq#626/wq#603 reopened with corrected notes' — about OTHER tickets) and wq#787 (a report quoting the metric's own SQL) are false positives.
field_in_error.verdict: 1.74 is a floor of unknown tightness, not a measurement. It is NOT a valid comparison point for any later rework figure. Do not plot it in a series.

replacement.description: Monotonic per-ticket column, bumped by wq on every terminal (done/rejected) -> in-flight (open/claimed/blocked) transition. Nothing a later `wq done`/`wq edit` writes can erase it.
replacement.pre-epoch_recoverability: NONE. The oldest queue.db backup (2026-08-14) predates the marker convention entirely and contains zero markers, so the lost reopens cannot be reconstructed from any surviving source. Three reopens (wq#433, wq#755, wq#760, all reopened 2026-08-22 04:36:00) were seeded by hand from evidence captured before their notes were overwritten; everything earlier is gone.
